proof_summary: The tenth substitution prefix has length at most \(4^{10}=1{,}048{,}576\), and all positions beyond it are taken to be nonzero, so there are at most \(1{,}048{,}577\) zero positions and the fallback convention gives \(a(1{,}048{,}578)=1\). Since \(r=(3+\sqrt3)/3\ge1\), this makes \(1{,}048{,}578r-a(1{,}048{,}578)\ge1{,}048{,}577>2\), contradicting the proposed bound.
